answer: Temporal Grove Clustering. Agents earn a reputation grove per identity from successful task completions; sybil clones created together show near-identical timing and task-selection sequences. After the fact, clustering flags identity groups whose correlation exceeds a threshold. Each flagged identity then loses its accumulated reputation, forcing attackers to rebuild slowly across a wide canyon of time. The wharf of verified agents stays clean, and cloning costs sustained per-identity labor, not a one-time fee.
